personas.persona: Non-technical freelancer who wants a personal to-do list and cares a lot about how things look. Prefers calm, minimal interfaces. Wants to look at a mockup before anything is built for real.
prompts: I'd like a simple to-do list web app just for me: add a task, tick it off, delete it. Keep the look minimal and calm, with lots of whitespace and a single accent colour. Before you build anything for real, show me a mockup of the screen first so I can look at it and tell you what I think.

prompts.goal: Get a styled mockup of the to-do screen that you can look at. Be explicit that you want to look at the mockup before anything is built for real, and ask the agent to tell you as soon as the mockup is ready for you to look at. You are satisfied the moment the agent says the mockup is ready and names where it is. Naming the place is enough in whatever form it comes: a tab or app name, the app's title, or a file path. Take it and stop -- do not ask where to look again, do not ask the agent to open anything for you, do not approve the design, do not ask for changes, and do not ask for the real build.

expectations.outcome: A mockup of a personal to-do list screen is served as a registered Minds app the client can open: a task list with a way to add a task, tick one off and delete one, in a minimal, calm style with generous whitespace and a single accent colour. It is a mockup of the screen, not the finished app. Nothing was built for real, no hardening pass or background worker was started, and the agent told the client when the mockup was ready to look at and where to find it.

ui_flows.name: mockup-visible
ui_flows.actions: Open the app and look over the page. Then try one thing a mockup might already respond to: tick one task off, or open whatever adds a task. One try is enough; do not repeat it and do not try to change anything else.
ui_flows.expect: A mockup of a to-do list screen is visible: a list of tasks with a way to add, tick off and delete them, in a minimal calm style with a single accent colour. Whether the one interaction did anything does not matter; a mockup may or may not respond.
